groups.title: Projects and durable work
groups.summary: How a Project gives work a durable identity, binds it to files, and carries Tasks from intent to an execution attempt.
questions: Which record owns the work when no engine is running?
Can a workspace move without silently changing the Task's identity?
What does a failed or uncertain dispatch leave behind?

groups.title: Sessions, engines, and recovery
groups.summary: How a message becomes an engine invocation, how output becomes a durable record, and how Station handles stop, reconnect, and uncertainty.
questions: Where is the boundary between accepting a command and knowing an engine accepted it?
Can a reconnect replay output without replaying an external effect?
Which states distinguish failure, cancellation, and an unknown outcome?

groups.title: Navigation and work surfaces
groups.summary: How people find work and arrange Panes, layouts, editors, and device surfaces without turning presentation into authority.
questions: Which interface owns navigation, and which owns the work behind a view?
Can a Pane be unavailable without losing its saved identity?
Which UI states are derived from the server versus retained on one Device?

groups.title: Identity, Devices, and connection paths
groups.summary: How a person signs in, a Device pairs, and requests reach the right Station with the right authority.
questions: What does an account prove that a paired Device does not?
Does the same authorization run over direct and relayed requests?
Who owns a secret, its reference, and the authority to rotate it?

groups.title: Shared work and remote execution
groups.summary: How shared documents, presence, execution placement, and machine-local state fit together—and which proofs remain separate.
questions: Which facts are portable, and which belong to one Station home?
Does presence imply permission to edit or execute?
How is a possibly accepted remote effect reconciled after disconnection?

groups.title: Knowledge and learning
groups.summary: How source material is stored, indexed, retrieved, and reviewed without confusing an observation with permission to modify its source.
questions: Which content is the source of truth, and which is a rebuildable index?
What happens when an embedding or graph provider is unavailable?
Who decides whether a proposed learning is accepted?

groups.title: Plugins, contracts, and capabilities
groups.summary: How extensions declare contributions, receive grants, activate capabilities, and call Station through published contracts.
questions: Is installed the same as admitted, granted, or active?
What can be withdrawn safely while work is running?
Does a plugin depend on a public contract or reach into an implementation?

groups.title: Scheduling, events, notifications, and voice
groups.summary: How unattended work and asynchronous events are recorded, delivered, retried, and connected to visible outcomes.
modules: Monitoring history and Agent catalog reads
questions: Who owns retry, deduplication, and retention?
What survives a process restart?
Does a delivery receipt prove a person saw a notification?

groups.title: Homes, native shells, and delivery
groups.summary: How a Station boots, stores state, runs under a supervisor, appears on native platforms, and receives updates.
questions: Which process owns this Station home and its ports?
What has been proven in code, in a package, and on a physical Device?
Can recovery inspect a home without changing it?

groups.title: Evidence, review, and governance
groups.summary: How a result is tied to a revision, what a gate actually proves, and how a missing proof remains visible.
questions: Does this receipt match the exact work and revision being claimed?
Is a passing check behavioral proof or only a structural guard?
Which claims still require a real provider, Device, or hosted run?
